# SaurioPDF — LLM Reference

PDF generation library for Deno, Node.js, Bun, and browsers.
Rust/WASM core (Krilla 0.8) + TypeScript builder API.
JSR: jsr:@sauriopdf/core  |  npm: sauriopdf  |  version: 0.2.0

---

## SETUP

**Deno / JSR**
```ts
import { init, PDF } from "jsr:@sauriopdf/core";
await init(); // idempotent — safe to call multiple times
```

**Node.js / Bun (npm)**
```ts
import { init, PDF } from "sauriopdf"; // npm install sauriopdf
await init(); // detects Node.js, reads .wasm via fs — no fetch needed. Requires Node ≥ 18.
```

**Browser**
```html
<script type="module">
  import { init, PDF } from "https://esm.sh/sauriopdf@0.2.0";
  await init(); // loads WASM via fetch, Liberation Sans + Mono already embedded
  const pdf = new PDF({ title: "My Doc" });
  pdf.h1("Hello");
  const bytes = await pdf.generate();
  const blob = new Blob([bytes], { type: "application/pdf" });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url; a.download = "doc.pdf"; a.click();
</script>
```

Edge runtimes (Cloudflare Workers, Vercel Edge, Deno Deploy) are NOT supported — WASM too large.

---

## THE BUILD

Single WASM build, ~5.4 MB, with Liberation Sans + Mono embedded — zero setup.
`loadFont()` / `loadFonts()` remain available for registering additional custom fonts.

---

## PDF CLASS

```ts
const pdf = new PDF(opts?: PDFOptions);

interface PDFOptions {
  title?:       string;
  author?:      string;
  subject?:     string;
  keywords?:    string[];
  pageSize?:    "A4" | "A3" | "A5" | "Letter" | "Legal" | "Tabloid"; // default: "A4"
  orientation?: "Portrait" | "Landscape";                             // default: "Portrait"
  margin?:      number | { top: number; right: number; bottom: number; left: number }; // default: 72
  gap?:         number;  // spacing added after each layout element, default: 8
  pdfa?:        "1a" | "1b" | "2a" | "2b" | "2u" | "3a" | "3b" | "3u";
}
```

**Fluent config methods (all return `this`)**
```ts
pdf.title("Doc").author("Alice").subject("Report").keywords("a", "b")
pdf.pageSize("Letter").landscape().portrait()
pdf.margins(50)                 // uniform
pdf.margins(40, 60)             // vertical, horizontal
pdf.margins(40, 50, 60, 50)     // top, right, bottom, left
pdf.noMargins()
pdf.gap(12)                     // change default spacing between elements
pdf.conformsTo("2b")            // PDF/A mode
```

**Read-only state getters**
```ts
pdf.cursor        // current Y position in points (useful when mixing layout + manual mode)
pdf.contentWidth  // page width minus left+right margins
pdf.pageWidth     // full page width in points
pdf.pageHeight    // full page height in points
```

---

## OUTPUT

```ts
await pdf.save("output.pdf");          // write file — Deno, Node.js, Bun
const bytes: Uint8Array = await pdf.generate(); // all runtimes including browser
```

---

## LAYOUT MODE

All layout methods return `this` for chaining. Cursor advances automatically. Page breaks
fire when content would overflow the bottom margin.

### Headings

```ts
pdf.h1(text, opts?)   // 28pt bold
pdf.h2(text, opts?)   // 22pt bold
pdf.h3(text, opts?)   // 17pt bold
pdf.h4(text, opts?)   // 14pt bold
// opts: { color?: ColorInput }
```

### Paragraph

```ts
pdf.p(text, opts?)
// opts: { size?, color?, align?, bold?, italic?, lineHeight?, font? }
// align: "Left" | "Center" | "Right" | "Justify"
// lineHeight: multiplier, default 1.4
// Wraps to content width, paginates automatically.
```

### List

```ts
pdf.list(items: string[], opts?)
// opts: { style?: "bullet"|"numbered", indent?: number, bullet?: string,
//         size?, color?, lineHeight?, font? }
// Default: bullet style with • character, indent 20pt
// Each item wraps to content width minus indent.
```

### Code block

```ts
pdf.code(source: string, opts?)
// opts: { font?, size?, color?, background?, padding? }
// Default font: "Liberation Mono", background: "#f6f8fa", size: 10, padding: 10
// Lines are NOT wrapped — use \n to break explicitly.
// Blank lines count toward height but emit no Text element.
```

### Callout / alert box

```ts
pdf.callout(message: string, opts?)
// opts: { type?: "info"|"warning"|"error"|"success", title?, size?, padding? }
// Renders a colored left-accent bar with title (bold) + message.
// Colors: info=blue, warning=amber, error=red, success=green
// Default title: "Info" / "Warning" / "Error" / "Success"
```

### Utilities

```ts
pdf.spacer(points = 16)         // vertical blank space
pdf.hr(opts?)                   // horizontal rule — opts: { color?, width? }
pdf.newPage()                   // commit current page, start new
pdf.pageBreak()                 // alias for newPage()
```

---

## TABLE

```ts
pdf.table({
  headers?: string[],
  rows: string[][],
  widths?: number[],         // ≤1 = fraction of content width (e.g. 0.4 = 40%)
                             // >1 = absolute points
                             // omit = auto-estimated from content
  columnAligns?: Align[],    // "Left"|"Center"|"Right"|"Justify" per column, default all "Left"
  striped?: boolean,
  borders?: boolean,         // default: true
  fontSize?: number,         // default: 11
  cellPadding?: number,      // default: 6
  rowHeight?: number,        // override auto height
  headerBg?: ColorInput,     // default: "#2c3e50"
  headerColor?: ColorInput,  // default: "#ffffff"
  stripedBg?: ColorInput,    // default: "#f4f6f8"
  rowBg?: ColorInput,        // uniform row background
  textColor?: ColorInput,    // default: "#111111"
})
```

Row heights computed dynamically from wrapped cell content. Tables auto-paginate — rows
that don't fit carry to the next page. Header is repeated on each continuation page.

---

## COLUMNS

```ts
pdf.columns(n: number, fn: (cols: PDF[]) => void, opts?)
// opts: { widths?: number[], gap?: number, divider?: boolean | ColorInput }
// widths: ≤1 = fractions, >1 = points. Default: equal width.
// gap: default 16pt between columns
// divider: vertical line between columns

pdf.columns(2, ([left, right]) => {
  left.h3("Left").p("Some text.");
  right.h3("Right").p("Other text.");
}, { gap: 24, divider: "#cccccc" });
```

Each column is a full PDF instance. After the callback, cursor advances past the tallest column.

---

## SECTION

```ts
pdf.section(opts, fn: (s: PDF) => void)
// opts: { background?, borderColor?, padding?, radius? }
// padding: number or { top, right, bottom, left } — default: 12

pdf.section({ background: "#f0f4ff", borderColor: "#93c5fd", padding: 16 }, (s) => {
  s.h3("Note").p("All layout methods work inside sections.");
});
```

Sections measure their content before rendering and reserve the full height at once.
They do not break across pages — if too tall, the section starts on a new page.

---

## HEADER / FOOTER

Set before adding content. Both repeat on every page.

```ts
pdf.header(height: number, fn: (ctx: HFContext) => void)
pdf.footer(height: number, fn: (ctx: HFContext) => void)

interface HFContext {
  pageNum:    number;  // 1-indexed
  totalPages: number;  // always correct — injected after all pages committed
  width:      number;  // full page width in points
  height:     number;  // band height as passed to header/footer
  add(...items): void; // same API as pdf.add()
}
// Coordinate system: (0, 0) = top-left of the band
```

```ts
pdf.header(40, (ctx) => {
  ctx.add(rect(0, 0, ctx.width, ctx.height).fill("#1a1a2e"));
  ctx.add(text("My Report").at(24, 14).size(14).bold().color("white"));
});

pdf.footer(24, (ctx) => {
  ctx.add(
    text(`Page ${ctx.pageNum} of ${ctx.totalPages}`)
      .at(0, 8).size(9).color("gray").center().maxWidth(ctx.width),
  );
});
```

---

## MANUAL MODE

```ts
pdf.add(...items: (Buildable | RawElement | Array<...>)[])
// Accepts builder objects, raw JSON elements, or arrays of either.
// Does NOT advance the cursor. Mix freely with layout mode.
```

---

## ELEMENT BUILDERS

### text(content, x?, y?, size?)

```ts
text("Hello", 50, 100, 14)
  .at(x, y)
  .size(n)
  .bold()
  .italic()
  .underline()
  .strikethrough()
  .color(ColorInput)
  .align("Left" | "Center" | "Right" | "Justify")
  .center()             // shortcut for .align("Center")
  .right()              // shortcut for .align("Right")
  .justify()            // shortcut for .align("Justify")
  .maxWidth(n)          // enables text wrapping — REQUIRED for alignment to work
  .opacity(0..1)
  .font("Liberation Sans")  // or use Font.Sans, Font.Mono, etc.
```

IMPORTANT: `.maxWidth()` enables wrapping AND alignment. Without it, text is single-line
and alignment has no effect. Always set maxWidth when centering or right-aligning text.

`text().buildAll(lineHeight?)` — returns one RawElement per wrapped line. Used internally
by layout mode. For manual mode, use `.build()` or pass directly to `pdf.add()`.

Underline and strikethrough are emitted as Shape.Line elements in `buildAll()`.

### rect(x, y, w, h, opts?)

```ts
rect(50, 100, 200, 80)
  .fill(ColorInput)
  .stroke(ColorInput, strokeWidth?)
  .strokeWidth(n)
  .round(radius?)    // rounded corners, default radius: 8
  .radius(n)
  .at(x, y)
  .dimensions(w, h)
```

### circle(x, y, radius, opts?)

```ts
circle(297, 400, 60)
  .fill(ColorInput)
  .stroke(ColorInput, strokeWidth?)
  .at(x, y)
  .radius(n)
```

### line(x1, y1, x2, y2, opts?)

```ts
line(50, 200, 545, 200)
  .color(ColorInput)
  .width(n)
```

### path(points, opts?)

```ts
path([[50,100], [200,100], [125,200]])
  .fill(ColorInput)
  .stroke(ColorInput, width?)
  .closed(true)     // default: true
  .open()           // shortcut for .closed(false)
  .point(x, y)      // add a point
  .points(arr)      // add multiple points
```

### image(data, opts?)

```ts
// data: Uint8Array — PNG, JPEG, or WebP (auto-detected from magic bytes)
image(pngBytes)
  .at(x, y)
  .width(n)
  .height(n)
  .size(w, h)
  .fit(maxWidth)    // scale to fit maxWidth preserving aspect ratio
```

### link(url, x, y, w, h)

```ts
// Clickable annotation — place over text to make it a hyperlink
link("https://example.com", 50, 450, 200, 18)
```

### imageSize(data: Uint8Array)

```ts
// Parse pixel dimensions from PNG, JPEG, or WebP header bytes without fully decoding.
const dims = imageSize(pngBytes); // returns { width, height } | null
```

---

## FONT CONSTANTS

```ts
import { Font } from "jsr:@sauriopdf/core";

// Available constants:
Font.Sans             // "Liberation Sans"
Font.SansBold         // "Liberation Sans Bold"
Font.SansItalic       // "Liberation Sans Italic"
Font.SansBoldItalic   // "Liberation Sans Bold Italic"
Font.Mono             // "Liberation Mono"
Font.MonoBold         // "Liberation Mono Bold"
Font.MonoItalic       // "Liberation Mono Italic"
Font.MonoBoldItalic   // "Liberation Mono Bold Italic"

// Usage
text("hello").font(Font.SansBold)
pdf.p("hello", { font: Font.Mono })
```

Both Liberation Sans and Liberation Mono are embedded in the full WASM build.

---

## FONT LOADING

```ts
import { loadLiberationSans, loadLiberationMono, loadBuiltinFonts,
         loadFont, loadFonts } from "jsr:@sauriopdf/core";

// Load all built-in fonts at their bundled path (redundant with the embedded
// Liberation set, but useful for re-registering custom Liberation-family builds)
await loadBuiltinFonts();

// Load Liberation Sans from a directory path (or URL prefix for browser)
await loadLiberationSans();                          // default: "fonts/liberation-fonts-ttf-2.1.5"
await loadLiberationSans("./my-fonts");              // custom local path
await loadLiberationSans("https://cdn.example.com/fonts"); // CDN

// Same for Liberation Mono
await loadLiberationMono("./my-fonts");

// Load a single custom font
await loadFont("MyFont Regular", "./my-font.ttf");

// Load multiple custom fonts
await loadFonts([
  { name: "MyFont Regular", path: "./regular.ttf" },
  { name: "MyFont Bold",    path: "./bold.ttf" },
]);
```

Font names follow the convention: family + variant suffix (" Bold", " Italic", " Bold Italic").
Rust maps variants by suffix to the correct font slot (bold, italic, bold_italic). Select the
variant with `{ bold: true }` / `{ italic: true }` on the base family name — `font: "MyFont Bold"`
is not a valid family and throws.

An unregistered font throws immediately at the layout call (p(), h1(), list(), …), not just at
generate()/save() — wrapping measures the string in its target font right away via measureChars().

Font subsetting is automatic — Krilla tracks every glyph drawn and subsets on finish().

---

## COLOR INPUT

```ts
type ColorInput =
  | string  // CSS named: "steelblue", "coral", "transparent", "white", "black" (100+ colors)
  | string  // hex: "#rgb", "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa"
  | [r: number, g: number, b: number]             // RGB, 0-255
  | [r: number, g: number, b: number, a: number]  // RGBA, rgb 0-255, a 0.0-1.0
```

---

## PAGE SIZES (points — 1pt = 1/72 inch)

```
A4:      595 × 842    A3:      842 × 1191    A5:      420 × 595
Letter:  612 × 792    Legal:   612 × 1008    Tabloid: 792 × 1224
```

Content area = page size minus margins (default 72pt = 1 inch each side).
Coordinate system: (0,0) = top-left of page, y increases downward, unit = points.
Coordinates are absolute page coordinates (not relative to margins).

---

## PDF/A

```ts
const pdf = new PDF({ pdfa: "2b" });
pdf.conformsTo("2b"); // fluent equivalent
// Levels: "1a", "1b", "2a", "2b", "2u", "3a", "3b", "3u"
// "2b" is the most common level for archival use
```

---

## WORKER POOL (optional — sauriopdf/pool)

Separate opt-in module, not imported by the main "sauriopdf" entry — zero cost unless used.

```ts
import { init, PDF } from "sauriopdf";
import { generateWithPool, initPool, terminatePool } from "sauriopdf/pool";

await init();     // still required — layout/wrapping runs on the main thread
await initPool(); // throws (does NOT silently fall back) if Workers aren't usable here

const pdf = new PDF();
pdf.h1("Hello");
const bytes = await generateWithPool(pdf); // rendered on a worker
terminatePool();
```

Runtimes: Deno/Bun/browser share the standard `Worker` API; Node.js uses `node:worker_threads`.
Known unsupported platform: Deno Deploy (isolate model, no OS threads) — `initPool()` rejects
there, by design; don't retry, just use the regular sync `generate()`.
Memory: N workers = N× the WASM footprint resident (each worker has its own WASM instance).
Custom fonts with the pool: use `registerFont` from `sauriopdf/pool`, not the regular one —
only that version propagates to live workers.

---

## quickPDF helper

```ts
await quickPDF("output.pdf", (pdf) => {
  pdf.h1("Hello").p("World");
});
// Creates PDF, runs builder, saves — all in one call
```

---

## COMPLETE EXAMPLE — Invoice

```ts
import { init, PDF, text, rect, link, Font } from "jsr:@sauriopdf/core";

await init();

const pdf = new PDF({ title: "Invoice #1042", margin: 60 });

pdf.header(40, (ctx) => {
  ctx.add(rect(0, 0, ctx.width, ctx.height).fill("#1a1a2e"));
  ctx.add(text("ACME CORP").at(24, 14).size(15).bold().color("white"));
  ctx.add(text("Invoice").at(ctx.width - 80, 14).size(12).color("#94a3b8"));
});

pdf.footer(24, (ctx) => {
  ctx.add(
    text(`Page ${ctx.pageNum} of ${ctx.totalPages}`)
      .at(0, 8).size(9).color("gray").center().maxWidth(ctx.width),
  );
});

pdf
  .h1("Invoice #1042")
  .p("Date: March 1, 2026  ·  Due: March 31, 2026", { color: "slategray" })
  .spacer(16)
  .section({ background: "#f8fafc", padding: 14 }, (s) => {
    s.p("Bill To:", { bold: true, size: 10, color: "slategray" });
    s.p("Globex Corporation\n742 Evergreen Terrace\nSpringfield, USA");
  })
  .spacer(16)
  .table({
    headers: ["Description", "Qty", "Unit Price", "Total"],
    rows: [
      ["Widget Pro",      "5", "$19.99",  "$99.95"],
      ["Consulting (hr)", "3", "$150.00", "$450.00"],
      ["Support Package", "1", "$299.00", "$299.00"],
    ],
    striped: true,
    headerBg: "#1a1a2e",
    widths: [0.45, 0.1, 0.2, 0.25],
    columnAligns: ["Left", "Center", "Right", "Right"],
  })
  .spacer(8)
  .p("Total: $848.95", { bold: true, align: "Right", size: 13 })
  .spacer(24)
  .callout("Payment due within 30 days. Bank transfer preferred.", { type: "info" });

await pdf.save("invoice.pdf");
```

---

## ARCHITECTURE NOTES (for contributors)

- ALL layout (cursor, wrapping, alignment, tables, page breaks) is TypeScript
- Rust/Krilla only receives pre-positioned elements via JSON — no layout in Rust
- Text wrapping: `wrapLines()` breaks text → `buildAll()` returns one RawElement per line
- Alignment: computed as x-offset by `alignmentOffset()` before sending to Rust
- Justify: extra space distributed across words; last line is Left
- Underline/strikethrough: emitted as Shape.Line elements alongside Text in `buildAll()`
- Tables: decomposed into rects + lines + text elements entirely in TypeScript
- Font subsetting: automatic via Krilla `subsetter` crate — tracks glyphs during `draw_text()`
- Page coordinate system: (0,0) = top-left, y increases downward, unit = points
- Header/footer injected AFTER all pages committed (so `totalPages` is always known)
- `shiftEl(el, dx, dy)` in `pdf-base.ts` shifts element coordinates for section/columns page breaks
- RawElement is a discriminated union: `{ Text } | { Image } | { Shape } | { Link }`

**Class hierarchy**
```
PDFBase (pdf-base.ts)      state, config, add/newPage/generate/save, shiftEl
  └─ PDFLayout (pdf-layout.ts)  h1–h4, p, list, code, table, img, callout, hr, spacer
       └─ PDF (pdf.ts)          section(), columns(), quickPDF()
```

section() and columns() stay in pdf.ts because they create `new PDF()` sub-instances.
Moving them to PDFLayout would create a circular import.

**Source files**
```
src/pdf-base.ts        PDFBase — document state, config, output
src/pdf-layout.ts      PDFLayout — auto-layout methods
src/pdf.ts             PDF — section, columns, quickPDF
src/elements.ts        All element builder classes + factory functions + imageSize()
src/table.ts           buildTableElements() — dynamic row heights, column alignment
src/layout.ts          wrapLines(), alignmentOffset(), estimateLineWidth(), estimateTextHeight()
src/types.ts           All public + internal types; RawElement discriminated union
src/colors.ts          parseColor() + CSS color name map
src/fonts.ts           Font name constants + BuiltinFont type
src/wasm.ts            WASM bootstrap (imports wasm/)
src/pool.ts            Optional worker-pool backend — not imported by mod.ts
src/worker-entry.ts    Script run inside each pool worker (own WASM instance)
lib/font-loader.ts     Font loading (registerFont from wasm/)
mod.ts                 Package entry point
pool.ts                sauriopdf/pool entry point (re-exports src/pool.ts)
wasm/                  Pre-built WASM with fonts embedded (5.4 MB)
fonts/                 Liberation Sans + Mono TTF files
rust-core/             Rust source — Krilla rendering pipeline
```
